newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday in active trading led by a continued rally in CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 103.28
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct at 102.66
Volume was high at 193 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in inflation-linked bonds.

"CPI-linked bonds continued to rise but at a slower pace. The main reason for the rise is that the CPI forecast for February rose from 0.6-0.9 percent to 1.1-1.2 percent," said a trader at Tachlit Investments.
But Yoram Ben-Yaeir of Ahrayut Investment Management said he was not sure rising inflation expectations could account for the strength of the rally.

"The rise of the inflation-linked bonds is very strange," he said. "Most analysts believe that the main reason is the change in inflation expectations, but this shouldn't have such a strong impact on long bonds."
"I believe the main reason is that the provident funds raised money they need to invest," he added.
The Tachlit trader said unlinked bonds and Makams also rose today because they offer yields attractive to investors who believe inflation will remain under control.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds rose sharply following the decline of the shekel against the dollar in the local forex market. On Tuesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3630 shekels against 3.3530 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
